answers.explanation: Tissue respiration takes place in the mitochondria, which release energy from glucose.
A tissue is a group of similar cells performing the same function.
The fern life cycle runs from prothallus, through gametes and egg cells, to the leafy sporophyte bearing sporangia and spores.
Platyhelminthes have a mesoderm layer, which coelenterates lack.
Hydra is diploblastic with two germ layers, while the tapeworm is triploblastic with a mesoderm.
The duration of sunlight determines when many plants in a habitat flower.
Termites undergo incomplete metamorphosis, in which the young resemble the adults.
An onion is a bulb because its stem is reduced and its leaves are thick and fleshy.
Stomata control the flow of air and water vapour into and out of the leaf's mesophyll.
Fungi lack chlorophyll, so they cannot make their own food and are heterotrophic.
Most photosynthesis takes place in the palisade parenchyma, which contains many chloroplasts.
The purple colour with sodium hydroxide and copper sulphate is the biuret test, which shows protein.
The hepatic portal vein carries blood from the alimentary canal to the liver.
Without oxygen, pyruvic acid is converted to carbon(IV) oxide and ethanol in yeast.
The malpighian tubules are the excretory organs of insects.
The atlas is the bone of the neck on which the skull rests.
Pancreatic juice contains amylase, lipase and trypsin.
Double fertilisation ensures the formation of both the embryo and the endosperm.
The yolk supplies nutrients to the developing embryo.
In hypogeal germination the cotyledons stay underground while the epicotyl elongates.
Parthenocarpic fruits develop without fertilisation of the ovule.
Sensory neurons carry stimuli from the body and internal organs to the central nervous system.
A climax community persists until the environment or climate changes.
A population is a collection of similar organisms that interbreed freely.
In a predator food chain, organisms become progressively smaller and more numerous along the chain.
The top level of the pyramid, H, contains the least stored energy.
The shark is a top predator that feeds on other consumers, so it is a tertiary consumer.
Mangrove swamps grow where a river meets the sea, in brackish water.
Clay has the finest particles of the soil types listed.
Malaria symptoms are caused by toxins released into the blood when red blood cells are destroyed.
All the daughters of a haemophilic father and a normal non-carrier mother receive the haemophilia allele and become carriers.
A child of a mother with genotype OO must have received an O allele from the mother and a different allele from the father, so the father is of group B.
Crossing RR with Rr gives 2RR and 2Rr offspring in equal numbers.
Offspring with a combination of traits not found in both parents show that the characters are not linked.
Uncontrolled out-crossing of pawpaw can introduce unwanted variability into the seeds.
Colour blindness is recessive and sex-linked, so women need two copies of the allele to be affected.
The hereditary material of the cell is DNA.
Fleshy tissues that store water and reduced leaves are adaptations of plants to dry environments.
Freshwater habitats have a very low and fairly stable salinity, so salinity is least likely to affect the animals living there.
Natural selection was developed independently by Darwin and Wallace.
Fossils in sedimentary rocks show remains of organisms characteristic of the time when the rocks were formed, which supports evolution.
